cohort: Pregnant women who delivered in a high-volume tertiary center between January 2013 and December 2016, including 101 women aged <15 years, 3611 aged 15-19 years, and 13,501 aged 25-30 years
finding: Adolescent pregnancy is associated with an increased risk of adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, including preterm delivery, low birth weight, and higher cesarean section rates.
mod_finding: This study examined maternal and neonatal outcomes of adolescent pregnancies, including the risk of cesarean section, but did not directly compare outcomes between different modes of delivery.
